principles: Collect only data necessary for an approved measurement purpose.
Prefer aggregate metrics when individual-level data is unnecessary.
Use synthetic data for development and testing where practical.
Document data sources, recipients, retention, and access controls.
Review vendors and processing arrangements before enabling new collection.

restricted_analytics_content: Patient names linked to healthcare activity
Appointment details that reveal sensitive information
Other personal or health information not approved for the analytics purpose
collection_controls: Do not send protected health information to general analytics tools without an appropriate, reviewed, and authorized arrangement.
Prevent sensitive information from entering URLs, event names, page titles, session replay, and error logs.
Review form analytics and session recording separately from ordinary page-view analytics.
Apply consent and notice requirements where applicable.
Do not assume pseudonymized data is automatically anonymous.
Use least-privilege access and defined retention periods.
Verify data flows before enabling new tracking.

incident_response.trigger: Sensitive information is unexpectedly recorded, transmitted, or exposed.
actions: Stop or contain the affected collection where authorized.
Notify the designated privacy or security owner.
Assess impact through the approved incident process.
Make notifications only through authorized people and procedures.
Verify the remediation before resuming collection.

validation: Inspect actual network requests and analytics payloads.
Verify consent behavior and tracking configuration.
Check that logs and dashboards do not expose sensitive content.
Re-test after analytics vendor or implementation changes.
